articles.title: Harvard Engineers Bacteria to Pull CO2 From Air Into Seawater 2.6 Times Faster
articles.excerpt: A genetically modified marine bacterium accelerates rock weathering by stripping rust from mineral surfaces, offering a new biological pathway for industrial-scale carbon removal.
articles.image_caption: Engineered bacteria designed for carbon capture. Harvard researchers modified E. coli bacteria to pull carbon dioxide from air into seawater at 2.6 times the natural rate.
articles.nri_angle: The research involves Indian-origin scientist Amogh Jalihal as co-author, and the carbon removal technology has implications for India's climate commitments and coastal infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple's M6 Mac Mini Gets First Pre-Order Discounts Ahead of September 22 Launch
articles.excerpt: Amazon has introduced up to $29 off the new M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini models, marking the first cash savings on Apple's latest desktop before it even ships.
articles.image_caption: An Apple Mac Mini computer. The M6-powered Mac Mini is available for pre-order ahead of its September 22 launch with early discounts from authorized retailers.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech professionals and developers eyeing a compact AI-capable desktop will find the M6 Mac mini's doubled Neural Engine and pre-order savings worth evaluating.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Notifies Rs 1.28 Lakh Crore Semicon 2.0 Scheme to Build End-to-End Chip Ecosystem
articles.excerpt: The government has formalized its most ambitious semiconductor policy, covering chip design to fabrication with $13 billion in incentives, minority stakes in startups, and a target of capturing 10 percent of the global chip market.
articles.image_caption: India has notified its Rs 1.28 lakh crore Semicon 2.0 scheme to build an end-to-end domestic chip ecosystem spanning design, fabrication, and equipment manufacturing.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin semiconductor professionals in Silicon Valley and global chip companies have a tangible pathway for ventures and investment in India's expanding chip ecosystem.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Copyright Office Rules AI-Generated Work Can Be Protected, but AI Cannot Be Named Author
articles.excerpt: In a landmark ruling on the DABUS artwork case, India takes a more permissive stance than the United States, holding that AI-generated output can meet originality requirements while restricting authorship to humans.
articles.image_caption: A copyright symbol displayed alongside branding and intellectual property concepts. India's Copyright Office ruled that AI-generated work can receive copyright protection, but the AI system itself cannot be named as author.
articles.nri_angle: India's ruling offers a more workable framework for AI-generated creative work than the US, relevant for Indian tech professionals and companies building with generative AI tools.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oracle Prepares Fresh Layoffs That Could Axe 3,000 Jobs in India as AI Spending Soars
articles.excerpt: The database giant is reportedly cutting 7,000 to 10,000 roles globally as it redirects billions toward cloud and AI infrastructure, with India bearing a significant share of the reductions.
articles.image_caption: The Oracle Corporation logo displayed at the company offices. Oracle is reportedly preparing to cut approximately 3,000 jobs in India as it redirects spending toward AI infrastructure.
articles.nri_angle: The cuts affect Indian tech professionals directly — Oracle operates major engineering and cloud hubs across six Indian cities, and the restructuring signals a wider shift in Big Tech's India hiring strategy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Pushes 'Carolina Principles' at G20 Tech Meeting as AI Giants Address World Leaders
articles.excerpt: Washington wants G20 members to avoid creating new AI regulatory bodies, unveiling non-binding guidelines at a gathering of tech titans and commerce ministers in North Carolina.
articles.image_caption: A G20 summit meeting. The United States pushed its 'Carolina Principles' framework at the G20 technology ministers' meeting as AI companies addressed world leaders.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American tech leaders and Indian-origin engineers at companies like OpenAI, Nvidia, and Google DeepMind have a direct stake in how global AI regulation shapes the industry's growth.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wipro Plans 10,000-Strong AI Specialist Force With 1,500 Embedded Engineers
articles.excerpt: India's fourth-largest IT company is building a dedicated AI capability, combining new hires, internal transfers and workforce reskilling under a $1 billion investment.
articles.image_caption: Wipro's corporate campus. The IT services company plans to build a 10,000-strong AI specialist workforce with 1,500 embedded engineers.
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT workers face both opportunity and displacement as AI skills become table stakes in the industry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI's Ad Business Hits $1 Billion Annualized Revenue as ChatGPT Ads Expand Globally
articles.excerpt: ChatGPT advertising reached a billion-dollar run rate after the U.S. pilot generated $100 million in its first six weeks. The Ads Manager has expanded to India, Europe and the Middle East.
articles.nri_angle: OpenAI's ad platform has expanded to India, creating new opportunities for Indian advertisers and tech companies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Targets Back-End Semiconductor and Analog Chips as Global Supply Chains Fragment
articles.excerpt: With billions in government incentives and facilities from Micron, Tata, and CG Power coming online, India is carving out a strategic niche in chip assembly, testing, and specialized analog production.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor wafer processing system inside a fabrication facility. India is positioning itself as a global hub for back-end chip assembly and testing.
articles.nri_angle: India's semiconductor push creates opportunities for diaspora tech professionals and companies seeking to diversify supply chains away from China.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bengaluru Startup Alteon Raises $2.5 Million to Build Wind-Powered Aircraft That Can Fly for a Year
articles.excerpt: Founded by 20-year-old Samay Sanghvi, Alteon aims to keep autonomous aircraft aloft indefinitely by harvesting energy from ocean winds — with maritime surveillance as its first use case.
articles.nri_angle: Indian startup Alteon, founded by 20-year-old Samay Sanghvi in Bengaluru, secures Silicon Valley backing for ambitious autonomous aircraft technology.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Aman Sanger, 25, Set to Be Worth $5.5 Billion After SpaceX Acquires His AI Startup Cursor
articles.excerpt: SpaceX agreed to acquire Anysphere, the company behind AI code editor Cursor, in a $60 billion all-stock deal — making its Indian-origin co-founder one of the youngest billionaires in tech.
articles.image_caption: Aman Sanger, 25-year-old Indian-American co-founder of Cursor, whose net worth is set to reach $5.5 billion after SpaceX acquires the AI coding startup for $60 billion.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American co-founder Aman Sanger, son of an IIT Bombay alumnus, becomes one of the youngest billionaires in tech history through AI coding startup Cursor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Algorithm Detects Hypertension and Diabetes From a Five-Second Facial Video
articles.excerpt: Japanese researchers demonstrate a machine-learning tool that screens for high blood pressure and diabetes using spectroscopic camera footage of the face, no cuffs or blood tests required.
articles.image_caption: Researchers have developed an AI system that can detect hypertension and diabetes markers from a brief facial video scan, potentially transforming routine health screening.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian populations face elevated rates of hypertension and diabetes; a contactless screening tool could improve early detection in diaspora communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Gandhinagar Uses Machine Learning to Find Materials That Could Convert CO₂ Into Industrial Fuel
articles.excerpt: Researchers screened 56 five-metal combinations using AI-accelerated simulations and identified three ultrathin catalysts that show promise for converting carbon dioxide into carbon monoxide without external electrical input.
articles.nri_angle: The research at IIT Gandhinagar showcases India's growing role in AI-driven scientific discovery and climate technology, an area of increasing collaboration between Indian institutions and the global research community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ten Indians and Indian-Origin Leaders Named to TIME100 AI 2026 List
articles.excerpt: From Sarvam AI's foundational models to IBM's enterprise strategy, Indian names span all four categories of TIME's annual ranking of the most influential people in artificial intelligence.
articles.nri_angle: Ten Indians and Indian-origin professionals spanning corporate leadership, research, healthcare, and policy recognized among the world's most influential people in AI
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Bombay-Incubated InspeCity Raises Rs 100 Crore to Build Satellite Service Stations in Space
articles.excerpt: The spacetech startup plans four in-orbit missions over the next 18 months to prove its autonomous satellite-servicing technology, with backing from Speciale Invest and investor Ashish Kacholia.
articles.image_caption: The InspeCity team at IIT Bombay, where the satellite-servicing startup was incubated. The company has raised Rs 100 crore to take its autonomous spacecraft technology from lab testing to in-orbit missions.
articles.nri_angle: Founded by IIT Bombay alumni, InspeCity represents India's growing claim in the global space economy. Its success signals that deep-tech hardware startups incubated at Indian institutions can compete with international players like Astroscale and Northrop Grumman.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Big Tech Books $160 Billion in Paper Gains From AI Investment Stakes
articles.excerpt: Alphabet and Amazon posted record quarterly profits, but much of the surge came from unrealized valuation gains on equity stakes in companies like Anthropic and SpaceX rather than core business revenue.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin executives and engineers play central roles at Alphabet, Amazon, and leading AI companies driving the investment and spending boom.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope Launches on Mission to Map Dark Energy and Discover New Worlds
articles.excerpt: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center on Sunday, beginning a five-year mission to survey the cosmos with a field of view 100 times larger than Hubble's.
articles.image_caption: The primary mirror of NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope in the cleanroom at Goddard Space Flight Center. The 2.4-meter mirror will enable infrared surveys with a field of view at least 100 times larger than Hubble's.
articles.nri_angle: NASA's Roman Space Telescope represents a major international scientific collaboration with publicly available data that will benefit researchers worldwide, including the growing Indian-origin astrophysics community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS and Rolls-Royce Run Jet Engine on 100% Hydrogen Through Full Flight Cycle
articles.excerpt: In an industry first, a modified Rolls-Royce Pearl 15 engine completed take-off, cruise, and landing on pure hydrogen at NASA's Stennis Space Center, capping a four-year propulsion program.
articles.image_caption: A Rolls-Royce Trent turbofan engine on a test bench at the company's facility in Derby, UK. TCS and Rolls-Royce have run a jet engine on 100 percent hydrogen through a full flight cycle.
articles.nri_angle: TCS's engineering partner role in a flagship Rolls-Royce aerospace program demonstrates Indian IT firms' expanding capabilities in core R&D, moving well beyond traditional outsourcing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS To Acquire Porsche's IT Consulting Arm MHP for $373 Million
articles.excerpt: India's largest IT services firm seals a five-year, $1.46 billion AI partnership with the German sports car maker alongside the acquisition of its 4,500-employee consulting subsidiary.
articles.image_caption: TCS CEO K. Krithivasan and Porsche CEO Michael Leiters at the signing of the acquisition and partnership agreement. TCS will acquire Porsche subsidiary MHP for $373 million alongside a $1.46 billion AI partnership.
articles.nri_angle: TCS's largest European acquisition underscores how Indian IT firms are moving beyond traditional outsourcing to own strategic consulting functions at marquee global brands.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Finds Six Ways to 3D-Print a NASA Rocket Alloy That Had Stumped Engineers for Years
articles.excerpt: Washington State University researchers used artificial intelligence to test just 40 of more than 100 million possible configurations, discovering settings that allow a high-performance copper alloy to be printed on standard commercial equipment for the first time.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin professors Susmita Bose, Amit Bandyopadhyay, and Jana Doppa at Washington State University led key aspects of the research that could democratize access to a critical aerospace material.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Venture Capital Bet Shifts From Software to Rockets, Chips, and Robots
articles.excerpt: Deep-tech startup funding in India rose 37% year-on-year even as overall venture capital declined, with Skyroot Aerospace becoming the country's first space-tech unicorn and government policy backing a long-term shift from code to hardware.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin venture investors and NRI engineers are increasingly backing and building deep-tech companies in India, bridging global expertise with the country's growing hardware ecosystem.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tech Mahindra and Uniphore Partner to Build Agentic AI Factory for Enterprise Clients
articles.excerpt: The Indian IT giant and Palo Alto-based AI firm will jointly develop and deploy autonomous AI agents for retail and financial services, starting with procurement and claims processing workflows.
articles.image_caption: Tech Mahindra has partnered with conversational AI firm Uniphore to build an agentic AI factory for enterprise clients.
articles.nri_angle: Tech Mahindra, one of India's largest IT firms, and Indian-founded Uniphore are jointly building AI infrastructure that could reshape how the Indian IT services sector delivers value globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta's India and Southeast Asia VP Sandhya Devanathan Joins OpenAI to Lead Regional Expansion
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin executive will oversee consumer growth, enterprise adoption, and regulatory engagement across Southeast Asia and Australia as OpenAI races to scale its Asia-Pacific presence
articles.image_caption: OpenAI's headquarters. The company has hired Sandhya Devanathan, Meta's former India and Southeast Asia VP, to lead its regional expansion.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech leader Sandhya Devanathan moves from one of the biggest roles in Indian tech leadership at Meta to a pivotal position at OpenAI, reflecting the outsized influence of Indian-origin executives in shaping global AI and social media strategy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Federal Judge Rules Pentagon's Blacklisting of Anthropic 'Illegal and Baseless'
articles.excerpt: In a 59-page ruling, U.S. District Judge Rita Lin found the Trump administration violated Anthropic's First and Fifth Amendment rights by designating the AI company a supply chain risk
articles.nri_angle: The ruling has major implications for Indian-American tech workers at AI companies navigating the intersection of government contracts and ethical AI development.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Unveils $100 Billion Louisiana Spaceport to Launch Thousands of Rockets Per Year
articles.excerpt: The world's largest launch complex will sit on 130,000 acres of Gulf Coast land in Vermilion Parish, with construction starting in 2027 and first Starship launch targeted for 2029
articles.nri_angle: The massive investment could create opportunities for Indian-American engineers and aerospace professionals, with SpaceX and the broader space industry increasingly recruiting from the diaspora's deep STEM talent pool.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Signs $45 Billion Compute Deal With British Startup Nscale
articles.excerpt: The six-year agreement for Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips at a West Virginia data center marks Anthropic's largest single compute commitment as AI firms race to lock in infrastructure.
articles.image_caption: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Anthropic has signed a $45 billion compute deal with British startup Nscale to expand its AI infrastructure.
articles.nri_angle: The compute arms race among AI companies has implications for the global tech workforce and Indian-origin engineers who make up a significant share of AI research teams at both Anthropic and its competitors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Orders 2 Million More Nvidia Chips in Tens-of-Billions AI Expansion
articles.excerpt: AWS will deploy Nvidia's next-generation Blackwell Ultra, Rubin, and Rubin Ultra GPUs through 2028, as Amazon pursues a dual strategy of building its own chips while deepening ties with Nvidia.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, California. Amazon has ordered 2 million additional Nvidia chips as part of a multi-billion dollar AI infrastructure expansion.
articles.nri_angle: The deal accelerates cloud AI infrastructure that powers applications used by enterprises globally, including Indian IT firms heavily invested in AWS services.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Ads in India With Over 50 Brands and Self-Serve Access From September
articles.excerpt: India becomes the third major market to get ChatGPT advertising, with WPP and Omnicom as launch partners and a self-serve ads manager opening September 4 for budgets starting at Rs 725 per day.
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech professionals and entrepreneurs in the diaspora who use ChatGPT daily will see ads on free tiers, while the self-serve platform creates a new channel for India-based businesses targeting NRI consumers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nvidia Forecasts 70% Revenue Growth for Fiscal 2028 as AI Demand Accelerates
articles.excerpt: The chipmaker reported $96.2 billion in quarterly revenue, more than double the year-ago period, and issued a rare forward-year guidance that far exceeded Wall Street projections.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The company reported quarterly revenue of $96.2 billion and forecast 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028.
articles.nri_angle: Nvidia is a major employer of Indian-American engineers in Silicon Valley and a key player in India's growing AI infrastructure market.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Maps Semiconductor Roadmap From 28nm to 3nm as Chip Design Push Accelerates
articles.excerpt: India targets 2-3nm chip production by 2032, with Renesas design center in Noida marking the country's first 3nm chip design facility and IIT Madras developing an indigenous 7nm processor.
articles.image_caption: A 12-inch silicon wafer used in semiconductor manufacturing. India has mapped a chip development roadmap from 28nm to 3nm as part of its domestic semiconductor push.
articles.nri_angle: India's semiconductor push creates opportunities for Indian-origin engineers in the US to contribute to the growing chip design ecosystem through companies like Qualcomm and ARM operating design centers in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wipro to Train 10,000 AI Specialists as It Deepens Google Cloud Partnership
articles.excerpt: Indian IT giant launches LIFT framework to help enterprises scale agentic AI, with 1,500 Forward Deployed Engineers leading deployment.
articles.nri_angle: Wipro's push to train 10,000 AI specialists signals continued demand for AI-skilled Indian engineers globally, reinforcing the Indian IT sector's role as a major employer of diaspora talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
